result.topic_en: Riemann's derivation of the Riemann invariants p, q for one-dimensional gas flow, the hodograph-type inversion to x, t as functions of p, q, the resulting linear equation for w, and its solution by the Riemann function method (Green's identity with boundary conditions, series solution).
result.transcription:
$-a^2\frac{\partial\log\varrho}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}+u\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}$ \quad $-\frac{\partial\log\varrho}{\partial t}=\frac{\partial\log\varrho}{\partial x}u+\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}$
[-$\frac{u+a\log\varrho}{4a}=p$-]
$u+a\log\varrho=4ap$ \quad $u-a\log\varrho=4aq$
$\frac{\partial p}{\partial t}=-(u+a)\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}$ \quad $\frac{\partial q}{\partial t}=-(u-a)\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}$
$dp=\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}dx+\frac{\partial p}{\partial t}dt$
$dq=\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}dx+\frac{\partial q}{\partial t}dt$ \quad $\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\frac{\partial q}{\partial t}-\frac{\partial p}{\partial t}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}=2a\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}=\Delta$
$\Delta\,dx=\frac{\partial q}{\partial t}dp-\frac{\partial p}{\partial t}dq$
$\Delta\,dt=-\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}dp+\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}dq$
$\Delta=2a\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial p}=\frac{-(u-a)}{2a\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}}$ \quad $\frac{\partial t}{\partial p}=\frac{1}{-2a\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}}$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial q}=\frac{u+a}{2a\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}}$ \quad $\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}=+\frac{1}{2a\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}}$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial q}=(u+a)\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}$ \quad $\frac{\partial x}{\partial p}=(u-a)\frac{\partial t}{\partial p}$
$\frac{\partial(x-(u+a)t)}{\partial q}=-2at$ \quad $\frac{\partial(x-(u-a)t)}{\partial p}=-2at$
$(x-(u+a)t)\,dp+(x-(u-a)t)\,dq=dw$ \quad $2a\,dw=(x-at)\,du-at\,d\log\varrho$ [?]
$\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p\partial q}-\frac{\partial w}{\partial p}+\frac{\partial w}{\partial q}=0$ \quad Grenzbedingungen [?]
$\int\omega\left(\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p\partial q}-\frac{\partial w}{\partial p}+\frac{\partial w}{\partial q}\right)\partial p\,\partial q=\int w\left(\frac{\partial^2\omega}{\partial p\partial q}+\frac{\partial\omega}{\partial p}-\frac{\partial\omega}{\partial q}\right)\partial p\,\partial q+\int\left(\omega\left(\frac{\partial w}{\partial q}+w\right)dp+w\left(\frac{\partial\omega}{\partial q}+\omega\right)dq\right)$
$\frac{\partial^2\omega}{\partial p\partial q}+\frac{\partial\omega}{\partial p}-\frac{\partial\omega}{\partial q}=0$ \quad $p=p')\ \frac{\partial\omega}{\partial q}+\omega=0$ \quad $q=q')\ \frac{\partial\omega}{\partial p}-\omega=0$ \quad $\omega=e^{(p-p')-(q-q')}\sum_0^\infty\frac{(p-p')^n(q-q')^n(-1)^n}{n!\,n!}$
$\frac{\partial^2 e^{q-p}\omega}{\partial p\partial q}+e^{q-p}\omega=0$ \quad $\frac{\partial e^{q-p}\omega}{\partial q}=0$ \quad $\frac{\partial e^{q-p}\omega}{\partial p}=0$ \quad $\int_{s,p'}^{s,q'}=\int_{s,p'}^{p',q'}+\int_{p',q'}^{s,q'}$
$(p=p',q=q')\ \omega=1$
$p=\text{const.}\ dq=\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}(dx-(u-a)dt)$ \quad $\left(1[-+-]-2at\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}\right)dq=d(x-(u-a)t)\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}$
